newsitem.title: USA: Senate rejects "killer" amendment to chemical pact.
newsitem.headline: Senate rejects "killer" amendment to chemical pact.

text.p: The Senate on Thursday took a step toward approving the global Chemical Weapons Convention by rejecting the first of four "killer" amendments which would have prevented U.S. ratification.

The amendment voted down would have barred U.S. ratification of the treaty until countries like Iraq, Libya and North Korea had signed up. The treaty is backed by President Bill Clinton but has been stoutly opposed by many Republicans.

The Senate voted to remove the amendment 71-29 although it had only needed a simple majority. This was four votes in excess of the number needed to provide a two-thirds majority for the treaty when the vote takes place on Thursday evening, encouraging supporters to believe they will win.
If any of the four "killer" amendments, inserted by a Senate committee, were allowed to remain it would render meaningless the vote on the overall resolution.
Sen Joseph Biden, a Delaware Democrat, said the amendment would have effectively "let the villains determine the rules of the road and determine U.S. foreign policy."

Senate Foreign Relations Committee Chairman Jesse Helms, a leading foe of the treaty, said the so-called rogue states posed the greatest chemical weapons threat to the United States and none were likely to sign on to the treaty. He has said that the non-participation by some states with chemical weapons programmes made the treaty meaningless.
